title: What AI is and where it fails
objectives: Recognise AI in tools and processes; name typical failure modes; know how to report a problem

title: Acceptable use of generative AI
objectives: Know the approved tools; the data classes each may receive; and what never to enter
grants: use of approved generative AI tools

title: Personal data in AI systems
objectives: Spot when a use case needs a DPIA addendum; record lawful basis per dataset; handle rights requests that touch models

title: Human oversight of decision-support systems
audience_roles: operators and reviewers of AI-supported decisions
objectives: Read the instructions for use; interpret scores and reason codes; resist automation bias; override and escalate correctly
grants: decide and override with the named system
evidences: EU AI Act Art. 14; EU AI Act Art. 26(2); NIST AI RMF MAP 3.4

title: Operating AI agents
objectives: Register an agent; scope its tools and spend; run and drill the kill switch; read agent traces
grants: owner or on-call for registered agents
evidences: EU AI Act Art. 14; NIST AI RMF MANAGE 2.4

title: Governance-as-code for builders
objectives: Write a policy card rule; add a blocking eval suite; emit evidence records; pass the release gate
evidences: ISO/IEC 42001 A.6; NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.4

title: AI incidents and reporting clocks
objectives: Open and triage an AI incident; run the reporting assessment; run a post-incident review
evidences: EU AI Act Art. 73; NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4.3

title: Buying AI
objectives: Flag AI in a purchase; send and assess the due-diligence questionnaire; turn gaps into contract conditions
evidences: ISO/IEC 42001 A.10; NIST AI RMF GOVERN 6.1

title: AI governance for executives and board members
objectives: Read the AI portfolio and risk position; know what decisions are reserved to the committee and board
